# Attestation test fixtures — vendored, not fetched

`workload_verifier_test.go` used to read these three files from
`../../secretvm-verify/`, a sibling checkout this repository does not contain,
does not ignore, and provisions from nothing. Ten tests therefore failed on
every clean checkout with `no such file or directory`. Ten tests that error on
a missing file and ten that pass look identical if only an exit code is read,
which is why this went unnoticed.

## Provenance

Upstream: `scrtlabs/secretvm-verify`, commit `592e434619ab4b3c90cb3adec0861e0984027ada`
(`artifacts_registry/tdx.csv` and `test-data/*`).

| `tdx.csv` | 99,553 | `0ecd5515de38345f966dd69258caf98a9716bb2cac7f5bbb0202642789d34db6` |
| `tdx_cpu_docker_check_quote.txt` | 10,013 | `12184fcf6e38f5e3b88b0f0b32e51eaa31136200eeef3f5d803c8c217454004b` |
| `tdx_cpu_docker_check_compose.yaml` | 9 | `d5f25b585a1d1972c6d65d1e04dc630a019bcb6ef6f1bb11eb4f8fe453e21961` |

## Why vendored rather than downloaded at test time

1. **The upstream repository has already disappeared once.** `.github/tee/secretvm.env`
   records it as removed, and the runtime registry URL was moved to a jsDelivr
   npm mirror because of it. It is reachable again today. A test that fetches is
   a test whose result depends on which of those two states the world is in.
2. **The npm/PyPI packages carry only one of the three files.** `secretvm-verify@0.13.0`
   ships `data/tdx.csv`; it ships no `test-data/`, so the quote and the compose
   have no package mirror to fall back to.
3. **A network fetch converts a real assertion into a skip.** The neighbouring
   `workload_rytn_test.go` already demonstrates the failure mode: it calls
   `t.Skipf` when its fixtures are absent, so it has been reporting green while
   testing nothing.

Fixtures are inputs, not expectations: none of them is regenerated by this
repository, so there is nothing here to keep in sync. Refresh them only when
the pin in `.github/tee/secretvm.env` moves, and re-record the digests above.

## What the fixtures have to satisfy

The quote's `MRTD`/`RTMR0`/`RTMR1`/`RTMR2` must match a row of `tdx.csv`, and
its `RTMR3` must equal `CalculateRTMR3(compose, row.rootfs_data)`. That
relationship is what `TestVerifyTdxWorkload_AuthenticMatch` asserts, so a
hand-made fixture set built with this package's own `CalculateRTMR3` would
assert only that the function agrees with itself. These are the upstream
reference verifier's own fixtures for exactly that reason.

`testdata/` is ignored by the Go toolchain, so none of this reaches a build.
